object_description: multi-layered school volume with a barn-like roof
design_condition: The scheme seeks varied relationships between interior and exterior spaces through embedded courtyards, but the volumetry remains insufficiently scaled and does not mediate the complex convincingly with its village context.

positive.statement: Very promising spatial relationships are offered between the upper corridor and the extra-high common room.

position.target: upper corridor and extra-high common room
position.rationale: Central upper-level marker approximates the vertical relationship between corridor and common room.

positive.statement: The access concept works towards a diverse relationship between the interior and exterior spaces.

position.rationale: Embedded openings and layered edges visibly connect internal and external zones.

negative.statement: The volumetry remains stuck in the schematic and can therefore develop the desired scale and naturalness only to a limited extent.

position.rationale: Irregular layered massing is directly visible across the plan and elevations.

negative.statement: The shape of the roof remains arbitrary.

position.rationale: Distinct upper roof outline is clearly visible in the top and south views.

negative.statement: The courtyards embedded in the volume cannot sufficiently moderate the transition from the school complex into the building structure.

position.rationale: Central voids and recessed outdoor spaces are identifiable in the top view.

negative.statement: The super-barn remains strangely alien as a new bearer of village identification.

position.rationale: Large barn-like upper mass is visibly distinct from the lower layered volume.
